text:
### Observed differences

- **The mandatory core reversed its order.** In the earlier window, A20, A22 and A23 (each in all 200 traces) sat at about 39–40% of the trace's length, ahead of A25 (about 45%) and A29 (about 65%), with A30 about two steps after A29. In the later window, A25 (about 39%) and A29 (about 58%) come first and A20, A22 and A23 (about 64%) follow, with A30 now about four steps after A29. Pairwise, A20 preceded A25 in about 99 of 100 earlier traces but A25 precedes A20 in all later traces; A20–A29, A22–A25, A22–A29, A23–A25 and A23–A29 flip the same way, and A29 now reaches A20 within one to three steps in essentially every later trace. [POS003, POS005, POS006, POS008, POS009, REL017, REL018, REL024, REL025, REL027, REL028, LAG003, LAG004]

- **The former tail activities now run at the front.** A19, A21 and A24 previously sat at about 67–69% of the trace, after the A25/A29 part of the flow; in the later window they sit at about 34–37%, before it. Their pairwise orders flipped accordingly: A29 used to precede A19, whereas A19 now precedes A20, A22, A23, A25 and A29 (about 44 in 100 later traces, never observed earlier); A20 used to precede A21, now A21 precedes A20, and the same reversal holds between A21 and A22/A23/A25/A29 and between A24 and A20/A22/A23/A25/A29. Participation shifted mildly: A19 up from about 31 to 44 in 100 traces, A21 down from about 38 to 28, A24 down from about 32 to 29. [POS002, POS004, POS007, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL026, REL029, REL030]

- **A02 became a frequent early step, and A40 now feeds it.** A02 appeared in about 8 of 100 earlier traces at a highly variable mid-trace position (mean about 0.51, wide spread) and in about 34 of 100 later traces, consistently at about 35% of the trace. A40, placed in every trace of both windows by the step-distance data, earlier sat one to three steps before A22; in the later window it immediately precedes A02 (one-step gap in about 62 later traces) and reaches A25 within two to three steps instead of about four, while A02 in turn precedes A20, A22, A23, A25, A29 and A30 in about 32 of 100 later traces, where earlier co-occurrence with these activities was about 8 of 100 with no fixed order. [OCC001, POS001, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, LAG001, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007]

- **A41 repeats more often.** It occurs in every trace in both windows, but mean occurrences per trace rose from about 1.5 to 1.8 and the share of traces containing repeats from about 33 to 40 in 100. [OCC002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a large-scale reordering of the case flow. In the earlier window a case typically ran A40 → A20/A22/A23 → A25 → A29 → A30, with A19, A21 and A24 (when they occurred, roughly three to four cases in ten) after that sequence; in the later window it typically runs A40 → A02 → A19/A21/A24 → A25 → A29 → A20/A22/A23 → A30. The core of this hypothesis rests on near-complete order reversals between activities observed in all 200 traces of both windows — for example A20 before A25 in about 99 of 100 earlier traces versus A25 before A20 in 100 of 100 later traces — together with directionally consistent position shifts for every affected activity and flipped precedence of A19, A21 and A24 against the whole block. [REL017, REL018, REL024, REL025, REL027, REL028, REL010, REL015, REL019, REL029, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]

Chance is an implausible explanation for the pattern as a whole: 48 control-flow items qualified where roughly 0.5 would be expected without a change, and the step-distance evidence corroborates the new arrangement directly — A29→A30 stretched from about two to about four steps, A40→A02 is now a single step in about 62 later traces, and A29→A20 occurs within one to three steps in essentially all later traces. [screening, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]

Limitations: positions and step distances are event-based, so no claim about clock time is possible; the reversal is relative, and the evidence cannot tell whether the early group was pushed later, the late group pulled earlier, or both; A02's earlier footprint is small (16 traces), so its previous placement is only roughly known [OCC001, POS001]. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that all cases switched wholesale between two pre-existing routings rather than one flow being reordered, since within each window the order on the affected pairs is nearly uniform (about 98–100 in 100 cases on one side) [REL017, REL025].

Other differences: A41 now repeats more often within a case (mean about 1.5 → 1.8 occurrences per trace; traces with repeats about 33 → 40 in 100), a repetition change the reordering hypothesis does not cover [OCC002]. The participation shifts of A19 (up, about 31 → 44 in 100) and of A21 and A24 (slightly down, about 38 → 28 and 32 → 29 in 100) accompany the reordering but are participation changes in their own right [POS002, POS004, POS007].
